$comment: Single source of brand truth for every public asset. Nothing in site/ or docs/marketing/ may hardcode a name, domain or package scope: they read these tokens. The name was decided on 2026-08-07 (Accordo) and the code surface renamed with scripts/brand-set.js; the tokens remain the single edit point, because a trademark screen could still force a second rename.

name.note: Chosen by the founder on 2026-08-07 over Pactar (more distinctive, but a live PACT word-mark in class 9) and Pactio (a live UK legal-tech namesake in adjacent software). Research and the eliminated candidates are in docs/marketing/NAME_VERIFICATION.md. The trademark screen has NOT been run — if it comes back badly, scripts/brand-set.js runs again with a different name.

domain.note: Registered by the founder on 2026-08-07. The registrar showed it as unavailable in a check run minutes earlier, which is consistent with that purchase — a DNS lookup the same morning had shown no A record, and this field warned that DNS silence is not proof either way. Ownership is the founder's statement; this environment can confirm the domain is registered, not to whom.

repository.note: Public since 2026-08-08, confirmed against the GitHub API rather than assumed. Flipping this one field is what turns indexing on: meta robots, robots.txt, the sitemap reference, both calls to action, the status banner and the codeRepository property in the structured data all follow it. vercel.json drops X-Robots-Tag in the same commit, and scripts/site-check.js refuses to let the two disagree.

npm.note: `create-accordo@0.1.0` is live: staged from CI through OIDC trusted publishing on 2026-08-19 (run 32224731197, provenance in the Sigstore transparency log) and approved by the founder with 2FA, then confirmed against the registry from this environment — the published shasum 69c2bc86eed9261f6f5ae293914065cedc1b17c1 matches the CI assembly and `latest` resolves to 0.1.0. So `npm create accordo` now scaffolds a working project. Three facts still stay separate: the framework arrives vendored, not as a dependency — upgrading means merging; the unscoped `accordo` name remains an empty 0.0.1 reservation, deliberately, because nothing installs the framework as a library; and the `@accordo` scope is claimed but deliberately empty — the organization exists (its registry org endpoint returns 200 with no packages, where a nonexistent org returns 404) and holds nothing, because the one package it was reserved for turned out to be unpublishable: the project MCP server composes from the generated indexes of the tree it runs in, so a published copy would answer about the wrong application (ADR-034). Publication remains a staged, human-approved action for every future version.

license.note: Confirmed by the founder on 2026-08-07 (ADR-023). MIT has been the repository licence since Milestone 0; what changed is that a distribution manifest may now assert it to a marketplace, which scripts/distribution-check.js refuses while the status is provisional.

promise: Describe your sales process to your coding agent; own the CRM it builds.
colorsNote: Inherited verbatim from apps/admin/public/styles.css so the site and the product it ships are visibly the same thing.
siteColorsNote: The public site's ground and its ink. Deliberately not in `colors` above: that block is the Admin's palette, inherited verbatim so the product and its site look like the same thing, and the site's warm paper is the one place the two intentionally differ. Read by site/assets/styles.css and by the theme-color meta tag, so the browser chrome on a phone matches the page instead of the Admin.
flowColorsNote: The four actors of the product's one decision, plus the green centre that is a valid business state. These are not decoration and not a second palette: violet is the agent, yellow the policy that stops it, coral the human who decides, cyan the evidence left behind, green the accord they reach. The site says a colour only when its actor enters the story, and the Accord Seal — assets/mark.svg — is those four arcs closing around the green. Kept here rather than as literals in the stylesheet because the mark, the social preview and the CSS must draw the same seal; site/assets/styles.css reads them as {{flow.agent}} and its siblings.

typography.sans: 'Bricolage Grotesque', 'Avenir Next', Avenir, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif
typography.mono: 'Spline Sans Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace
typography.display: 'Bricolage Grotesque', 'Avenir Next', Avenir, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif
typography.note: Both faces are vendored under site/assets/fonts as latin-subset variable woff2 and declared with @font-face in styles.css. They are not loaded from a font CDN: the site ships `font-src 'self'` (vercel.json), and a page that reaches a third party to render its own headline is the same kind of borrowed runtime the framework refuses. Every family ends in a system stack, so a blocked or slow font degrades to a rendered page rather than invisible text. Licences and attribution: site/assets/fonts/OFL.txt.
